Services.Name: Winter Tire Changeover
Services.Summary: We swap your tires for winter tires before the snow and back again in the spring, and we can store your off-season set.
Services.Body:
Winter tires grip better than all-season tires once it gets cold. Their rubber stays soft in freezing weather, and their tread is cut to bite into snow and slush. Most tire makers suggest switching when the temperature stays below about 45 degrees.

## When to switch

Plan your changeover before the first real snow, which in Fargo often comes in October or early November. Tire shops get busy once the first storm hits, so earlier is easier. Switch back in the spring, since winter tires wear faster on warm, dry roads.

## What we do

- Swap your tires, or mount and balance them on your wheels
- Check the air pressure and tread on every tire
- Store your off-season tires here at the shop, so you don't have to haul them home
- Help you pick a new set of winter tires if yours are worn

Walk-ins are welcome for tire work. Want more grip on ice? Ask about [tire siping](/services/tire-siping/).

Services.Name: Wheel Alignment
Services.Summary: Computerized four-wheel alignment for cars and pickups, domestic or foreign, plus 3-axle computerized truck alignment.
Services.Body:
Potholes, frost heaves and curbs can knock your wheels out of line, and our roads have plenty of all three by spring. Wheels that are out of line wear tires unevenly and can make your vehicle pull to one side.

## Signs you need an alignment

- Your vehicle pulls left or right on a straight road
- The steering wheel is off center when you drive straight
- Your tires wear faster on the inside or outside edges
- You just bought new tires or hit a big pothole

## What we align

- Cars and pickups, domestic or foreign, with computerized four-wheel alignment
- Trucks, with 3-axle computerized truck alignment

Our ASE-certified technicians check and adjust your alignment so your tires last longer and your vehicle drives straight.

Services.Name: Nitrogen Inflation
Services.Summary: Nitrogen tire inflation is available. Ask us whether it's right for your vehicle.
Services.Body:
We fill tires with nitrogen instead of regular air. Nitrogen leaks out of a tire more slowly than air and stays dry inside it, so your tires hold the right pressure longer.

## What it does in the cold

Cold weather still lowers tire pressure, about 1 psi for every 10 degrees, with nitrogen or with air. Nitrogen helps by keeping the rest of the loss small, so your tires spend fewer days running low.

## Who it helps most

- Pickups, trailers and equipment that sit between uses
- Farm and commercial tires that carry heavy loads
- Anyone who doesn't check their tire pressure often

Read more in our post, [Nitrogen in your tires: why it helps in a North Dakota and Minnesota winter](/blog/nitrogen-tire-inflation/).
Services.Photo Alt: Branick nitrogen tire inflation machine at the shop

Services.Name: Tire Siping
Services.Summary: Siping cuts thin slits across the tread for extra traction on ice and snow.
Services.Body:
Siping cuts many thin slits across a tire's tread. As the tire rolls, each slit opens a little and adds a biting edge, so the tire grips better on ice, packed snow and wet roads.

## Who it helps

- Drivers who want more winter grip without studded tires
- Cars, pickups and SUVs that see a lot of ice and packed snow
- Work trucks and fleets that run in every kind of weather

## Good to know

- Siping works best on new tires or tires with plenty of tread left.
- Not every tire is a good fit, so ask us about yours.
- It pairs well with a [winter tire changeover](/services/winter-tire-changeover/) before the snow flies.

Cold is hard on batteries. On a below-zero morning a battery has much less starting power, so one that worked fine in October may not start your vehicle in January.

## Battery check and replacement

- We'll check your battery before the cold sets in.
- If it's weak, we'll replace it with the right battery for your vehicle and install it for you.

## Wiper blades

Ice, salt and slush wear wiper blades out fast. We sell and install Michelin wiper blades, so you can see clearly through the next storm.

Call or stop in before the first cold snap.

Blog Posts.Title: When should you switch to winter tires in Fargo?
Blog Posts.Summary: Switch before the first real snow, once it stays below about 45 degrees. Here's how to time it and what to check.
Blog Posts.Search Title: When to Switch to Winter Tires in Fargo, ND | Fargo Tire Service
Blog Posts.Search Description: Most tire makers say to switch when it stays below about 45 degrees. Here's how to time your winter tire changeover in Fargo, and what to check first.
Blog Posts.Text:
The first real snow in Fargo often comes in October or early November, and tire shops get busy as soon as it hits. Here's how to time your winter tire changeover so you're ready before then.

## The 45-degree rule

Most tire makers suggest switching to winter tires when the temperature stays below about 45 degrees. That's not about snow. It's about rubber.

All-season tires are made for a wide range of weather, and their rubber stiffens as it gets cold. Stiff rubber doesn't grip as well, even on dry pavement. Winter tires use a softer rubber that stays flexible in freezing weather, and their tread has deeper grooves and more edges to bite into snow and slush.

So the best time to switch is when the cold settles in, not after the first storm. In Fargo, that usually means sometime in October.

## Signs it's time

- Mornings are below freezing most days.
- Daytime highs are staying in the 40s or lower.
- The forecast calls for the first snow.
- Your tire pressure light came on during a cold morning. [Cold lowers tire pressure](/blog/nitrogen-tire-inflation/), so it's a good reminder to check your tires anyway.

## Check your winter tires before they go back on

If you stored winter tires from last year, look them over first.

- **Tread.** Winter tires lose snow grip as they wear. For a quick check, put a quarter upside down in the tread. If you can see the top of Washington's head, the tread is down to about 4/32 of an inch, and it's time for a new set.
- **Damage.** Look for cracks, bulges or cuts in the sidewall.
- **Age.** Rubber hardens over time, even on tires that sat in storage. The last 4 digits of the DOT code on the sidewall show the week and year the tire was made.

Not sure about yours? We check the air pressure and tread on every tire when we do a changeover.

## Put winter tires on all 4 wheels

Winter tires on only the front or only the back leave the other end of the vehicle with less grip. That can make it slide or spin out when you brake or turn on snow. Put them on all 4 wheels.

## A second set of wheels saves time

If your winter tires are mounted on their own wheels, each changeover is a quick swap instead of taking tires off and on the rims twice a year. If your vehicle has tire pressure sensors, the second set of wheels needs sensors too, or the pressure light may stay on all winter. We can order [aftermarket wheels](/services/wheels/) if you need a set.

## When to switch back

Once the temperature stays above about 45 degrees in the spring, switch back to your all-season or summer tires. Winter tires wear faster on warm, dry roads, so taking them off on time helps them last more winters.

## Winter tire changeover at Fargo Tire Service

- We swap your tires, or mount and balance them on your wheels.
- We check the air pressure and tread on every tire.
- We can store your off-season tires here at the shop, so you don't have to haul them home.
- We can help you pick a new set of winter tires if yours are worn.

No appointment needed for tire work. Stop in at 2020 Main Ave in Fargo, call (701) 232-7177, or read more about our [winter tire changeover](/services/winter-tire-changeover/). Want even more grip on ice? Ask about [tire siping](/services/tire-siping/).

Blog Posts.Title: Nitrogen in your tires: why it helps in a North Dakota and Minnesota winter
Blog Posts.Summary: Nitrogen won't stop the cold from lowering your tire pressure, but it helps tires hold pressure longer and stay dry inside.
Blog Posts.Search Title: Nitrogen Tire Inflation for Cold Weather | Fargo Tire Service
Blog Posts.Search Description: Nitrogen helps tires hold pressure longer and keeps them dry inside. Here's what that means in a North Dakota and Minnesota winter.
Blog Posts.Text:
The first real cold snap of the fall turns on a lot of tire pressure lights in Fargo and Moorhead. Nitrogen won't stop that, but it does help your tires hold their pressure better the rest of the winter. Here's what it does, and what it doesn't.

## What a nitrogen fill is

The air in your tires is already about 78% nitrogen. The rest is mostly oxygen, plus a little water vapor. A nitrogen fill replaces most of that oxygen and moisture with more nitrogen.

## Why it helps tires hold pressure

Every tire slowly loses pressure through the rubber, and oxygen works its way out faster than nitrogen does. In a year-long test by Consumer Reports, tires filled with nitrogen lost about a third less pressure than tires filled with air.

Nitrogen is also dry. Air from a compressor carries some moisture, and that water stays inside the tire. A dry fill means less moisture to rust steel wheels or corrode valve stems over time, and less oxygen working on the rubber from the inside.

## What it means in a North Dakota and Minnesota winter

Cold lowers tire pressure by about 1 psi for every 10 degrees the temperature drops. That's true for nitrogen and air alike. A tire set to 35 psi in a 70-degree shop will read close to 26 psi on a 20-below morning.

Nitrogen helps with the part you can control. Your tires start the winter at the right pressure and lose less on top of what the cold takes, so they spend fewer days running low. Low tires wear faster on the edges, use more fuel and don't grip as well on snow and ice.

A few habits matter more than what's in the tire:

- Check your pressure once a month and after a big temperature drop.
- Check it cold, before you drive, and use the numbers on the sticker in the driver's door jamb, not the number on the tire.
- If the pressure light comes on during the first cold morning, it's usually the cold, not a leak. Fill the tires to the door-sticker pressure. If the light keeps coming back, stop in and we'll check for a leak.
- Topping off with regular air is fine. It just dilutes the nitrogen a little.

## Who gets the most from nitrogen

- Pickups, trailers and equipment that sit for weeks between uses.
- Farm and commercial tires that carry heavy loads, where steady pressure helps them wear evenly.
- Anyone who doesn't check their pressure often. Nitrogen gives you more room for error.

If you check your pressure every month, the difference is smaller. Nitrogen isn't magic, but in a place where winter already pulls pressure down, keeping the rest of the loss low is worth it.

## Nitrogen at Fargo Tire Service

We fill tires with nitrogen at the shop at 2020 Main Ave in Fargo. No appointment needed for tire work. Ask about it when you buy tires, or read more about [nitrogen inflation](/services/nitrogen-inflation/).

FAQ.Question: Do I need an appointment?
FAQ.Answer: No. Walk-ins are welcome for tire work.

FAQ.Question: Do you have a waiting room?
FAQ.Answer: Yes. Our [waiting room](/waiting-room/) has free WiFi, a TV and a restroom.

FAQ.Question: Do you come to job sites and farms?
FAQ.Answer: Yes. Our fully equipped service trucks, with cranes, handle tire work at your site. Call (701) 232-7177.

FAQ.Question: Do you take after-hours calls?
FAQ.Answer: Yes. We offer after hours service, after-hour rates will apply.

FAQ.Question: What tire brands do you sell?
FAQ.Answer: Michelin, Goodyear, BFGoodrich, Titan, Uniroyal, Hercules and Toyo, plus hard-to-find sizes. We can get any brand you want.

FAQ.Question: Does road hazard coverage come with new tires?
FAQ.Answer: Free road hazard coverage comes with passenger and light truck tires you buy here.

FAQ.Question: Do I have to replace all 4 tires on an all-wheel-drive vehicle?
FAQ.Answer: Usually, yes. On most all-wheel-drive vehicles, all 4 tires need to be close to the same size and tread depth. A new tire next to worn ones turns at a different speed, and that can strain and damage the drivetrain. Many automakers say to replace all 4 at once, or to keep the tread depths within a small amount of each other, so check your owner's manual. Stop in and we'll measure your tread and tell you what your vehicle needs.

FAQ.Question: Do you align vehicles?
FAQ.Answer: Yes. We do computerized four-wheel alignment for cars and pickups, plus 3-axle computerized truck alignment.

FAQ.Question: Where are you located?
FAQ.Answer: 2020 Main Ave in Fargo, North Dakota.

Duane "Andy" Anderson bought the business in 1972, and it has been family owned and operated ever since. In 1979 a new building addition doubled the alignment department, and computerized alignment was added.

Andy's sons joined the business, Paul in 1985 and Roger in 1986. Paul and Roger have managed the business since 1998.
